name: Re-entry + Field Day
note: Stay here as long as the goal remains useful. Review progress and recovery before advancing; no calendar automatically changes your block.
ready: Review consistent training, recovery, and tolerance of running/landing before progressing. Do not use a date as proof of readiness.
keep: Muscle, strength, aerobic work and mobility.
next: Redirect event preparation toward lasting body control.
markers: Repeat A/B with stable technique; record recovery and tolerated athletic practice.

name: Foundation + Body Control
focus: Develop relative strength alongside the lifting foundation.
note: Stay here as long as the goal remains useful. Review progress and recovery before advancing; no calendar automatically changes your block.
ready: Review A/B consistency, controlled bodyweight variations, recovery between sessions, and available time.
keep: Giant lifting, conditioning, modest athletic exposure and mobility.
next: Build the capacity to handle a deliberate increase in training opportunities.
change: Body control becomes the supporting emphasis in place of event preparation.
markers: Compare controlled pull-up/push-up variations and A/B performance at similar effort.

name: Giant Expansion
focus: Prioritize muscle development and address weak points.
note: Stay here as long as the goal remains useful. Review progress and recovery before advancing; no calendar automatically changes your block.
ready: Review whether the extra day is sustainable without declining main-lift performance or persistent fatigue.
keep: Hypertrophy stays central; retain the engine, movement and relative strength.
next: Support more purposeful speed, jumping and athletic development.
change: Main sessions offer more volume; a third lifting day is an optional tool.
markers: Look for repeatable rep/load progress without the optional day reducing A/B performance.

name: Athlete Development
focus: Develop acceleration, landing quality and body control.
note: Stay here as long as the goal remains useful. Review progress and recovery before advancing; no calendar automatically changes your block.
ready: Review repeatable controlled landings, tolerated running exposure, stable lifting performance and recovery. Faster or longer sprint work needs an individual progression.
keep: At least the two core resistance sessions, aerobic work and mobility.
next: Arrive at coached skill training with a more durable physical base.
change: Athletic practice becomes the main supporting emphasis.
markers: Track repeatable practice quality and coach feedback while maintaining lifting.

name: Combat Foundations
focus: Build a coached combat skill on the physical base.
note: Stay here as long as the goal remains useful. Review progress and recovery before advancing; no calendar automatically changes your block.
ready: Review coach feedback, class consistency, joint tolerance and recovery before adding more classes or another discipline.
keep: Two resistance anchors and mobility; adjust accessory fatigue around classes.
next: Combine skill with broader real-world physical capabilities.
change: A beginner class replaces some accessory or conditioning time.
markers: Review class attendance, coach feedback and recovery into your next lifting day.

name: Broad Capability
focus: Develop one additional practical capability at a time.
note: Stay here as long as the goal remains useful. Review progress and recovery before advancing; no calendar automatically changes your block.
ready: Review coached competency, sustained training consistency and the ability to add a skill without losing the established base.
keep: Muscle, strength, coached skills, aerobic work and small athletic exposures.
next: Identify the weakest useful capability for the next specialization.
change: Select supervised water skills, loaded movement or practical instruction.
markers: Record demonstrated competency and whether your established training remains sustainable.

name: Lifelong Giant
focus: Maintain strengths while developing the weakest useful capability.
note: Stay here as long as the goal remains useful. Review progress and recovery before advancing; no calendar automatically changes your block.
ready: There is no graduation date. Review progress, enjoyment, recovery and real-life demands; select the next emphasis deliberately.
keep: The qualities you have earned, with ongoing muscle and strength development.
next: Repeat the cycle: raise the weakest stat and maintain your strengths.
change: Choose a focused emphasis at each review and revisit earlier phases as needed.
markers: Compare progress in that emphasis, maintained strengths and fit with everyday life.
